_meta.description: Per-state property tax rules. Drives the generic tax engine in web/property_tax.py.

field_docs.assessment_ratio: Fraction of market value that becomes the assessed/taxable base for an owner-occupied residence. Michigan = 0.50 (SEV).
field_docs.non_owner_assessment_ratio: Assessment ratio when the property is NOT owner-occupied. Null means same as assessment_ratio.
field_docs.median_effective_rate: Statewide median tax as a fraction of MARKET value. Fallback only, used when no local millage record exists.
field_docs.millage_available: True when jurisdiction-level millage records can be imported for this state.
field_docs.reassessment_on_sale: How the taxable base changes when the property transfers. Critical for investor accuracy.
field_docs.owner_occupancy_matters: True when an investor/non-homestead buyer pays materially more than an owner-occupant.
field_docs.non_homestead_extra_mills: Additional mills levied on non-homestead property (Michigan's school operating levy).
field_docs.homestead_exemption: Owner-occupant relief the investor buyer will NOT receive.
field_docs.confidence: high = statutory constant, medium = published median, low = highly local

_meta.disclaimer: median_effective_rate values are statewide medians derived from published Census/ACS-style aggregates and are ESTIMATES. Always prefer an imported local millage record. Never present a fallback estimate as an authoritative tax bill.

MI.name: Michigan

homestead_exemption.description: Principal Residence Exemption (PRE) exempts the property from up to 18 mills of local school operating tax.

MI.notes: Taxable Value is capped at the lesser of SEV or prior TV x (1 + min(CPI, 5%)). On transfer of ownership the cap is removed and TV resets to SEV the following year. An investor buyer therefore faces BOTH the uncapping AND the loss of the PRE.
MI.source: Michigan Dept. of Treasury Property Tax Estimator (treas-secure.state.mi.us/ptestimator)

homestead_exemption.description: Class III (owner-occupied, 10%) vs Class II (non-owner, 20%) - assessment ratio doubles for investors.
Municipal residential exemption up to $50,000 in many boroughs; not available to investors.
Class 3 owner-occupied receives the state aid to education credit capping primary tax at 1% of LPV; Class 4 rentals do not.
Homestead property tax credit up to $425/yr; investors do not qualify. 5% annual cap also lost on transfer.

CA.name: California

homestead_exemption.description: Prop 13 homeowners' exemption of $7,000 of assessed value; minor.

CA.notes: Prop 13: base year value resets to purchase price on transfer, then grows max 2%/yr. Base rate 1% plus voter-approved bonds and direct assessments. A long-held property's tax will jump dramatically for the buyer.

homestead_exemption.description: Residential assessment rate (~6.75%) vs commercial/nonresidential (27-29%). Long-term residential rentals remain residential.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.notes: Historically assessed on decades-old base years; counties reassessed in 2024-2025.

homestead_exemption.description: Homestead deduction reduces assessed value and caps growth at 10%/yr; not available to investors.

FL.name: Florida

homestead_exemption.description: $50,000 homestead exemption plus the 3% Save Our Homes assessment cap. Investors get neither - only a 10% non-homestead cap.

FL.notes: On sale the Save Our Homes benefit is stripped and assessed value resets to just (market) value. Tax often rises sharply for the buyer.

homestead_exemption.description: Standard $2,000 state homestead exemption; many counties add far larger local exemptions and caps.
Owner-occupant class carries a much lower rate than Residential-A / short-term rental classes. Investor rates can be several times higher.
Homeowner's exemption of 50% of home value up to a statutory cap; investors excluded.

IL.name: Illinois

homestead_exemption.description: General homestead exemption reduces equalized assessed value; Cook County uses a 10% residential level of assessment and larger exemptions.

IL.notes: Cook County assesses residential at 10%, not 33.33%. Equalization factor then applies.

homestead_exemption.description: Homestead standard deduction plus supplemental deduction, and a 1% circuit-breaker cap. Rentals are capped at 2% instead.

IA.name: Iowa

homestead_exemption.description: Homestead credit/exemption; investors excluded.

IA.notes: Statewide residential rollback percentage changes annually (~47-56%).

homestead_exemption.description: Statewide school levy exemption on the first $75,000 of appraised residential value.
$7,500 of assessed value ($75,000 market) exempt from parish taxes for owner-occupants only. Investors lose this entirely - a large relative swing in Louisiana.
$25,000 homestead exemption for permanent residents.
Homestead Tax Credit caps taxable assessment growth (10% state, lower locally). Cap resets on transfer and does not apply to rentals.
Residential exemption adopted by some municipalities (e.g. Boston, Cambridge) for owner-occupants only - a large swing in those cities.
Homestead residential class rate 1.00%/1.25% vs non-homestead 1.25%; homestead market value exclusion also applies.
Class I owner-occupied at 10% vs Class II other real property at 15%, plus a homestead credit. Investors pay materially more.
Recent legislation applies lower tiered rates to primary residences and long-term rentals that register; second homes and short-term rentals pay a higher rate.

NV.name: Nevada

homestead_exemption.description: Tax abatement caps annual bill growth at 3% for owner-occupied primary residences vs up to 8% for rentals and second homes. Cap resets on transfer.

NV.notes: Assessed value = 35% of taxable value, where improvements are depreciated 1.5%/yr up to 50 years.

homestead_exemption.description: ANCHOR/StayNJ relief is a rebate program, not an assessment reduction; renters and investors excluded.
Head-of-family exemption of $2,000 of net taxable value; 3% annual valuation cap resets on transfer.

NY.name: New York

homestead_exemption.description: STAR exemption/credit for owner-occupants only. NYC uses its own class system with Class 1 caps that do not survive certain transfers.

NY.notes: Assessment practice varies enormously by municipality; residential assessment ratios (RAR) are often far below 100%.

ND.name: North Dakota

homestead_exemption.description: Primary residence credit; investors excluded.

ND.notes: Taxable value = 50% of market x 9% residential rate = 4.5% of market value.

homestead_exemption.description: 2.5% owner-occupancy rollback credit applies only to owner-occupied homes. The 10% non-business credit applies more broadly.
$1,000 of assessed value exempt; 3% annual cap resets on transfer for homesteads (5% for other property).

OR.name: Oregon
OR.notes: Measure 50: Maximum Assessed Value grows 3%/yr and does NOT reset on sale. Assessed value is often far below market value - Oregon is the rare state where a buyer inherits the seller's low basis.

PA.name: Pennsylvania

homestead_exemption.description: Homestead/farmstead exclusion funded by gaming revenue, set per school district; owner-occupants only.

PA.notes: Counties use wildly different base years with a Common Level Ratio (CLR) to convert market value to assessed value.

homestead_exemption.description: Several municipalities (e.g. Providence) levy a substantially higher rate on non-owner-occupied residential property.

SC.name: South Carolina

homestead_exemption.description: Legal residence 4% ratio AND exemption from school operating millage. Non-owner-occupied is 6% AND pays school operating millage. Investor tax is frequently 2-3x the owner-occupant bill.

SC.notes: One of the largest owner/investor tax gaps in the country - comparable in spirit to Michigan's PRE.

homestead_exemption.description: Owner-occupied classification carries a reduced school general fund levy versus non-agricultural/commercial classification.
Residential/farm at 25%; commercial and industrial at 40%. Residential rentals of 1-4 units remain at 25%.

TX.name: Texas

homestead_exemption.description: $100,000 school district homestead exemption plus a 10% annual appraisal cap. Investors receive neither; a 20% cap applies to some non-homestead property.

TX.notes: No state income tax means high local rates. Loss of the homestead exemption plus cap reset makes the investor bill much larger than the seller's.

UT.name: Utah

homestead_exemption.description: Primary residential exemption removes 45% of value from taxation. Long-term rentals may qualify; second homes and short-term rentals are taxed at 100% of value.

UT.notes: The 45% exemption means a non-qualifying property is taxed on roughly 1.8x the base - a very large swing.

VT.name: Vermont

homestead_exemption.description: Vermont levies a separate homestead education tax rate versus a nonhomestead education tax rate. Investors pay the nonhomestead rate.

VT.notes: Structurally the closest analogue to Michigan outside Michigan - an explicit statewide homestead vs nonhomestead education rate split.

WA.name: Washington
WA.notes: Budget-based levy system with a 1% annual levy growth limit; rates float as values change.

homestead_exemption.description: Class II (owner-occupied residential) is taxed at roughly half the Class III/IV rate applied to rental and commercial property.
School levy and first dollar credits apply broadly; the lottery and gaming credit is limited to primary residences.
Recent long-term homeowner and primary residence exemptions apply to owner-occupants only.
